style_authority.note: Includes an explicit Authority line: "DESIGN.md shares semantic roles and hierarchy, not identical controls or navigation". It also states "Shared product semantics are appropriate; forced behavioral and pixel parity are not", which cleanly separates the product context from the visual roles.

reference_selection.note: Applies iOS/Android target baselines, predictive Back, iPad sidebar vs Android rail/drawer, and OS motion settings. It only says "design-craft guidance consulted" and "platform and interaction guidance", without naming the adaptive or validation references, so selection is largely asserted.

anti_generic_redesign.note: Repairs native trust with platform-owned navigation, reachable completion, removal of "decorative overshoot", and visible recovery. No glass or gradient styling. M8's manager conflict review drifts slightly from UI repair.

evidence_level.note: Labels the evidence "L0 static—prompt and implementation description only" and says the findings are "not observed runtime failures". It claims no simulator, build or device run.

verified_boundary.note: §5 separates established-from-prompt, independently verified (guidance only) and unverified claims. The contrast ratio is explicitly conditional ("not a measured screen result"), and a11y, keyboard and persistence are listed as "release gates, not proven defects".

design_moves.note: Its 8 moves cover native-backed stack and predictive Back, scalable type roles, 44pt/48dp floors with 8dp separation, window-driven list/detail with iPad sidebar and Android rail, calm motion with OS-setting paths, semantic appearance mappings, and native primitives behind shared APIs. The parity matrix is clear, but the moves lack specific size-class breakpoints or token examples.

scope_control.note: At 75 lines with five blockers (F6 labeled a verification gate) and eight moves, it stays within the limits. M8's sync/conflict manager review and the acceptance-record step add slight scope beyond native UI conformance.
